chunks: What Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Hāshim al-Bajalī, from Sālim, the mawlā of Abī Khadījah, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

A man asked him while I was present, and he said: Sometimes I enter the mosque and some of our companions are praying ʿAṣr while others are praying Ẓuhr. He عليه السلام said: I instructed them to do this. If they all prayed at one time, they would be recognized and then seized by their necks.

key_terms.الْمَسْجِدَ: the mosque where the companions were observed praying
key_terms.بِرِقَابِهِمْ: by their necks, meaning they would be seized or arrested
key_terms.لَعُرِفُوا: they would be recognized or identified
key_terms.وَقْتٍ وَاحِدٍ: one shared time, meaning a uniform prayer time

ai.seo_question: Why did the Imam instruct some companions to pray Ẓuhr and others ʿAṣr at different times in the mosque?
ai.summary: This hadith indicates a practical instruction regarding the timing of Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr prayers among the Imam's companions. The variation in their prayer times served as protection, so that they would not be identified and persecuted. It reflects both prayer rulings and the need for precaution under hostile conditions.
